name: Audio Buffer Tuner
description: Speeds up channel startup for low-bitrate (usually audio only) streams by lowering the TS-proxy prebuffer for chosen Channel Groups.
author: CtznSniiips

fields.label: Prebuffer chunks for matching groups
fields.help_text: Each chunk is ~256KB. Dispatcharr's normal default is 4 chunks (~1024KB) before a channel goes active. Lower values start faster but leave less margin against provider hiccups — fine for steady low-bitrate audio, riskier for video. (Shown here as a static default before the plugin is enabled; once enabled this range follows Dispatcharr's actual configured default.)

fields.label: Chunk size for matching groups (KB)
fields.help_text: Dispatcharr's normal chunk size is ~256KB. Smaller chunks mean less data has to accumulate before the first chunk (and each subsequent one) is ready, on top of whatever the prebuffer-chunk-count setting saves. Going very low increases Redis write frequency — usually fine for one or two audio channels, but don't push it to the floor across dozens of channels. Only applies to buffers created after you save this — already-running channels keep their current chunk size until they restart.

fields.label: The Channel Group picker appears here once the plugin is enabled and can read your groups from the database.

actions.label: Show current status
actions.description: Reports which Dispatcharr processes have the override installed, current settings, the groups it applies to, and the most recent overrides actually applied to a channel.
